symptom: Initial local Linux receiver-admission tests incorrectly required recvmsg returned msg_flags == 0; Python/Linux returned MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC in the output flags on valid single-FD receives, failing three otherwise valid fixture cases. The corrected fixture masks this known flag, rejects MSG_CTRUNC/unknown bits, and separately asserts the received FD is non-inheritable. This was a test assumption, not a production failure.
lesson: Do not infer recvmsg success from a zero output flag word when MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC is requested. In the observed Python/Linux binding the input flag appears in msg_flags on successful receive. The security property is the received FD's actual non-inheritable state, while MSG_CTRUNC and unexpected output bits must still be denied.
guardrail: For Linux/Python SCM_RIGHTS fixtures, permit only the documented MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC flag in the returned mask; fail closed on MSG_CTRUNC, unexpected flags, missing or extra FDs, and inheritable received FDs. Close all received FDs even when rejecting. Reuse the embedded-Python newline framing LEARN; do not connect this research-only test to production, Current BUY/LINE/public/automated betting, protected N2 or automatic recovery.
